tasks.short: Check the wholesaler delivery, store it, check expiry dates, record stock differences and report shortages to the pharmacist.

steps.what: Pharmacy technician unpacks incoming supplies and verifies quantities against invoices and delivery notes
Pharmacy technician stores the medicines, fridge items first
Pharmacy technician checks shelves for outdated medications with a monthly paper list
Pharmacy technician enters stock differences and missing items in the pharmacy system
Pharmacy technician tells the pharmacist about stock needs and shortages
Pharmacist decides on alternatives for medicines that are not available

tasks.design: The technician scans each pack's 2D code on receipt; the pharmacy information system ({OTHER}) matches it with the wholesaler's electronic delivery note, records batch and expiry date, and flags differences and missing items. Expiry checks become a monthly list of what expires soon, and shortages show on the pharmacist's screen; storing and decisions on alternatives stay manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expiry dates were not captured on receipt, so shelves were checked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Pharmacy systems read pack codes and take electronic delivery notes from wholesalers.
tasks.still_hard: Fridge items and controlled drugs need careful handling; shortages need the pharmacist's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a damaged pack or a cold-chain break at delivery.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; checks are faster and complete.

reach.role: pharmacy assistant at a hospital pharmacy
reach.learn: Whether scanning on receipt suits ward supply.

evidence.claim: Integrations and records apps replace paper logs and spreadsheets in data entry and logging tasks.
EU rules on falsified medicines require checking the pack's unique code before dispensing.

assumptions: Boundary: from delivery to shortages reported; ordering is outside.
Input contract: electronic delivery notes sent by the wholesaler; pack codes scanned by the technician on receipt; fallback is the paper delivery note.
Pharmacist time is outside the technician's savings.
unknowns: Whether the wholesaler sends electronic delivery notes.
research_questions: Does expired stock fall after expiry dates are captured on receipt?

incremental.description: Pharmacy technician handles packs whose code will not scan.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Pharmacies whose wholesaler sends no electronic notes keep checking by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer phone calls about repeat prescriptions, ready status and questions, look up records, pass questions on and log requests.

steps.what: Pharmacy technician answers telephones for repeat prescription requests
Pharmacy technician answers calls asking whether medicine is ready
Pharmacy technician looks up the patient's medication record during the call
Pharmacy technician responds to questions or passes them to the pharmacist
Pharmacy technician writes call-backs and requests in free text in the system

tasks.design: Patients request repeat prescriptions in the pharmacy's patient app linked to the pharmacy information system ({OTHER}) and get a message when medicine is ready, so those calls fall away. Calls that remain use a structured request form, and medication questions stay with the technician and pharmacist; no voice bot answers patients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every repeat request and status question came by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Pharmacy patient apps take repeat requests and send ready messages.
tasks.still_hard: Older patients keep calling; medication questions need a person.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a caller is confused about their medicine and getting the pharmacist on the line.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; the phone rings less.

reach.learn: Whether app requests cut calls at both ends.

evidence.claim: Pharmacy patient apps take repeat requests and send ready notifications.
Health data are special-category data under the GDPR.
Patient chatbots must disclose that they are AI; this design uses no chatbot.

assumptions: Boundary: from incoming calls to requests logged; dispensing is outside.
Input contract: repeat requests entered by patients in the app; ready status set when the bag is checked; fallback is the phone.
Patient time on the app is outside the technician's savings.
Medication questions and record lookups do not change.
unknowns: Share of patients who would use the app.
research_questions: How many calls per day disappear with app requests and ready messages?

already_counted.description: Pharmacy technician checks app requests before processing.

incremental.description: Pharmacy technician helps patients set up the app.
Pharmacy manager keeps app settings and texts current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Pharmacies with many older patients who prefer the phone see fewer calls move to the app.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find out what the customer needs, locate items, answer simple questions by protocol, check interactions and refer to the pharmacist.

steps.what: Pharmacy technician asks what the customer needs
Pharmacy technician walks to find items on the shelves or in the back
Pharmacy technician answers simple questions with the standard advice protocol
Pharmacy technician checks by hand the customer's record for clashes with the chosen product
Pharmacy technician refers customers to the pharmacist for medication information

tasks.design: The counter screen of the pharmacy information system ({OTHER}) shows stock and shelf location for over-the-counter items, and scanning the product with the customer's record open runs the existing medication surveillance on it. Asking, advising by protocol and referring stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Over-the-counter sales were not linked to the customer's record, so clashes were checked by memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch pharmacy systems run national drug database surveillance with minimum settings set by the pharmacists' association.
tasks.still_hard: Customers may not want their purchase linked to their record; advice stays a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a 'simple' question hides a medicine problem and calling the pharmacist.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; checks are automatic when the customer agrees.

reach.learn: Whether linked checks are possible outside a pharmacy.

evidence.claim: Dutch pharmacy systems run national drug database surveillance on interactions, contraindications and doses with minimum settings from the pharmacists' association.
Health data are special-category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the customer's question to referral; dispensing is outside.
Input contract: shelf locations kept by the technicians in the system; OTC sale linked to the record only with the customer's consent; fallback is memory.
Pharmacist time is outside the technician's savings.
Questions, protocol advice and referral do not change.
unknowns: Share of customers who agree to link purchases.
research_questions: How often does the linked check catch a clash?

incremental.description: Pharmacy technician keeps shelf locations current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Customers who refuse to link purchases keep the manual check.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scan prescriptions and products at the till, explain co-payments, take payment and count the till at closing.

steps.what: Pharmacy technician scans prescription bags and products at the cash registers
Pharmacy technician explains co-payments and the deductible
Pharmacy technician accepts payment from customers in cash or by card
Pharmacy technician counts and reconciles the till at closing

tasks.design: The till in the pharmacy information system ({OTHER}) sends amounts straight to the card terminal, card takings reconcile automatically with the payment provider, and cash is kept small, so closing is a short count. Scanning and explaining co-payments stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Amounts were keyed into a separate card terminal and all takings were counted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Tills link to card terminals, and payment providers send daily settlement files.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining the deductible to an upset customer takes time and tact.

reach.learn: Whether automatic card reconciliation removes daily differences.

evidence.claim: Tills can send amounts to card terminals and reconcile card takings from settlement files.
Businesses keep their administration and receipts under national tax rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from scanning to the till count; bookkeeping is outside.
Input contract: settlement files from the payment provider set up by the pharmacy manager; fallback is a manual count.
Pharmacy manager time is outside the technician's savings.
Scanning and explaining do not change.
research_questions: Do till differences fall with linked terminals?

incremental.description: Pharmacy technician handles terminal link failures.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Pharmacies with many cash customers keep long counts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The pharmacy technician keeps customer contact, protocol advice and careful handling; receiving, calls and till work shrink.
skills_to_grow: Helping patients use the pharmacy app
role.ambitious_version: A technician who spends the day advising customers instead of answering status calls and counting shelves.
